problem:
The sum of all twelve $12$th roots of unity is equal to$\,$
{{field-1}}.
worked_solution:
Recall that the principal $12$th root of unity is 

$$
z={e}^{2\pi \text{i}/12}\ne 1,
$$

and that any $12$th root of unity is of the form ${z}^{k}$ for $k=0,1,…,11.$  Also, we have ${z}^{12}=1.$

Using the formula for the sum of a geometric sequence, we obtain that the sum of all twelve roots is 

$$
\begin{aligned}1+z+{z}^{2}+⋯+{z}^{11} & =\frac{1\cdot (1-{z}^{12})}{1-z} \\  & =\frac{1\cdot (1-1)}{1-z} \\  & =\frac{1\cdot 0}{1-z} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
